In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism by which IL-10 mediates the induction of T cell tolerance in LCMV-infected mice.
the mechanisms that lead to the development of tolerance in chronic viral infections.
the mechanisms by which virus-specific T cells are anergized during persistent viral infections.

the early production of IL-10 is a necessary but not sufficient condition for virus-specific T cell tolerance.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IL-10 is an important player in the early stages of LCMVClone 13-induced virus-specific tolerance, although other mechanisms are also involved.

the generation of functional memory T cells in the context of persistent infection requires the early suppression of the effector T cell response.
